newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed flies to NATO headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Lebed flies to NATO headquarters.

text.p: Russian security tsar Alexander Lebed flew to Brussels on Sunday to inform NATO officials about the steps Moscow could take if the Western alliance goes ahead with its expansion plans, Interfax news agency said.
Lebed, secretary of President Boris Yeltsin's policy-making Security Council, has accused NATO of failing to adapt to the realities of the post-Cold War era.
The trip to Brussels is his first outside the former Soviet Union, with the exception of Afghanistan.

"A. Lebed opposes NATO expansion and will inform the leadership of the alliance about possible negative consequences of such a step," Interfax quoted an unnamed senior Security Council official as saying before Lebed left.

The reserve general, who has made strong anti-Western statements in the past, told Germany's Der Spiegel news magazine that planned NATO expansion to include Moscow's former allies in east and central Europe was "unacceptable" to Russia.
The interview was released on Saturday ahead of its publication on Monday.
"The threat supposedly posed by the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact five or ten years ago no longer exists," Lebed said. "But NATO formulates and realises its aims and tasks just as it did before."
Other Moscow officials have said they oppose NATO expansion but none has detailed countermeasures Moscow might take.
Political analysts have said Russia could renege on obligations under the Conventional Forces in Europe treaty to balance its Warsaw Pact forces with those of NATO.
The treaty was agreed shortly before the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991.
